resources.string: Factory signing identities
Create, back up or restore recoverable app signing keys
Choose a recoverable identity before signing a NEW app. Its encrypted backup belongs to you. Existing non-exportable identities cannot be exported, converted or replaced.

Keep your passphrase and backup safely, separately. Losing the passphrase or your only backup may permanently prevent app updates after device loss or uninstalling Jarvys. This backs up only the signing identity, not projects or app data. A saved backup is not a verified restore.
Application ID, e.g. com.example.myapp
Create NEW recoverable identity
Export encrypted identity backup
Import selected identity backup
Review identity and version floor
Choose an action. Files are selected manually using Android. No automatic upload is performed.
Identity management requires Android 8 or later.
Close
This application already has an identity. It cannot be replaced or converted. Export is available only for an existing recoverable identity.
A ready recoverable identity is required. Existing AndroidKeyStore identities are non-exportable, even if their key is missing. No replacement was created.

Create a distinct recoverable signing key for %1$s only. First choose where to save its encrypted backup; then confirm a passphrase and approve creation. No key is generated before your final approval, and the local identity is not saved until the backup write succeeds. Your chosen document provider receives the encrypted backup and filename; it may sync them to its service. Cancel if you do not want that destination.

Export the existing recoverable signing identity for %1$s. Choose a destination and a passphrase for this backup. Its known release version is only a snapshot; later releases are not included. Your chosen document provider receives the encrypted backup and filename; it may sync them to its service. Existing non-exportable identities cannot be exported.
Choose backup destination
Android could not open the document picker. Nothing was generated or imported.
Cancelled. No pending approval remains. Check any selected destination for an empty or incomplete file before retrying.

Enter a strong, unique passphrase of 12–1024 characters. Jarvys cannot recover a lost passphrase. It is used only in this native screen and is not retained. The keyboard app can still observe what you type; use a trusted keyboard.
Backup passphrase
Confirm backup passphrase
I understand the loss risk and approve saving this encrypted identity to the destination I selected. I will keep a separate safe copy and test restoration independently.
Approve and save backup
Confirm the backup and loss-risk acknowledgment to continue.
Use matching passphrases of 12–1024 characters, not blank. Please enter them again.

The backup could not be saved and read back exactly, or local identity creation failed. A selected file may be empty, partial or already complete. If a complete backup was saved but local creation failed, import that same backup to recover; do not replace an existing identity. Restoration has not been verified.

The encrypted backup was read back exactly and the new recoverable identity was saved. This does not verify restoration. Test the backup on an independent installation before relying on it, and retain the passphrase separately.
The encrypted backup was written, closed and read back exactly. This does not verify cloud sync, future availability or restoration. Keep the passphrase separately and test restoration independently.
Enter the selected backup’s passphrase to inspect its identity. Unlocking does not import or approve it. The file is bounded and its integrity, certificate and key are checked before preview.
Unlock and preview
The backup could not be unlocked or validated. Check the passphrase and file; it may be damaged, unsupported or inconsistent. No identity was imported.
Approve identity restore

Application ID: %1$s

Certificate SHA-256:
%2$s

Last version recorded in this backup: %3$d

Compare this fingerprint with your previous signed APK or trusted receipt. A matching existing recoverable identity can be repaired; a legacy or different identity cannot be replaced.

The backup may predate newer releases. After import, the latest release remains UNKNOWN and signing is blocked until you explicitly review and reconcile the version floor. No missing projects, app data or release receipts are reconstructed.
Approve this identity import

The matching identity was imported. The latest release version is UNKNOWN. Use “Review identity and version floor” after checking your latest APKs and receipts. Signing stays blocked until you resolve the version floor.

Application ID: %1$s

Certificate SHA-256:
%2$s

Known version floor: %3$d
History status: %4$s

Check every later signed release, including unpublished or publication-unconfirmed APKs, on your other devices and release services. Enter at least the highest version you find. An old backup alone cannot establish the latest release. This is your explicit declaration, not independent verification by Jarvys.
Resolved locally or explicitly declared
UNKNOWN after restoration
Highest previously signed version code
I checked my latest signed releases and receipts, and declare this floor is at least their highest version. I understand that Jarvys cannot independently prove no later release exists.
Approve declared version floor
Acknowledge your release-history check and enter a valid version no lower than the known floor.
Your declared version floor was saved. Future signing must use a strictly higher version. This declaration does not independently verify the latest release or restore missing receipts.
The operation could not be completed safely. Check the application ID and identity state. Existing identities are not replaced; no detailed key or provider error is displayed.
Working locally. Keep this screen open. Leaving revokes pending approval; an atomic save already in progress may still complete.

Pending approval was revoked when this screen was interrupted. An atomic save already started may have completed. Review the identity before retrying; a saved encrypted backup may need importing if local creation did not finish.
Enter a lowercase, dot-separated application ID with 2–16 segments and at most 127 characters. Android and Jarvys IDs are reserved.
